resourceName: Carbon fixation project associated with LtPF conservation scenario of riparian strip enlargement
description: This improved forest management (IFM) project was developed by the Cree First Nation of Waswanipi (CFNW) for both objectives: 1) added carbon fixation from trees and 2) enhanced wildlife habitat protection from logging activities. This project started in 2016 and consists in improving Cree standards to protect more areas while decreasing commercial harvesting on their land to achieve more greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions reductions. The project area represents the new conservation areas (enlarged buffer strips) under the improved Cree standards whose total area is 3 879 hectares (ha), excluding areas without merchantable and operable timber volumes. The project boundary represents Category I lands of Waswanipi located in the province of Quebec, Canada, whose total area is 60 358 ha. Prior to 2016, harvesting operations have been implemented throughout the project boundary for many years in respect to provincial and Cree standards. In 2016, thanks to the potential financial incentive to be granted through the sale of carbon credits, the CFNW adopted a new land-use plan, known as wildlife concerns, extending most of the buffer strips of riparian zones of previous Cree and provincial standards, therefore prohibiting harvesting activities in the project area. Simultaneously, the CFNW significantly reduced the harvest level in the project boundary. Both measures have had a negative impact on the earnings of the CFNW from stumpage fees. It is expected that the project scenario will generated GHG emission reductions by allowing the biomass of standing trees to fix more CO2 than the baseline scenario, where carbon is emitted in the short term by short-lived biomass fraction decomposition, wood waste combustion, logging slash decomposition, and in the long term by gradual emission of the carbon fraction sequestered in the harvested wood products over time. Ex-ante projections of the net cumulative GHG emissions reductions are 267 121 tCO2eq over 37 years with buffer deduction.
